name: identity_temporal_imprint
label: The Echo of What Was
poeticVision: The player will feel the desperate utility of past actions, but also the painful, creeping emptiness as each 'echo' extracts a piece of Lyra's very being. It's a visceral choice between immediate survival and the slow erosion of self, making the world slightly less familiar, her own memories a little hazier. A powerful tool that saves her life at the cost of who she is, a heart-wrenching trade.

parameters.name: echo_instance_scene
parameters.description: The PackedScene for the Echo instance (Node3D with MeshInstance3D, GPUParticles3D, StaticBody3D, CollisionShape3D).

parameters.name: max_history_size
parameters.description: Maximum number of past states (echoes) to store in history.

parameters.name: echo_duration
parameters.description: Duration in seconds for which an activated echo remains visible and interactive.

parameters.name: identity_cost_per_echo
parameters.description: The amount of 'identity' lost (0.0 to 1.0) each time an echo is activated. Emitted via 'identity_cost_incurred' signal.

verdict: A brilliant echo of desperation, this mechanic weaves the very fabric of identity into the brutal calculus of survival, making every choice a haunting sacrifice.
impact: This mechanic will force players into agonizing decisions, constantly weighing immediate survival against the slow, irreversible loss of Lyra's identity. Every use of an echo will be a moment of desperate utility, followed by a subtle but profound sense of emptiness, making the player viscerally feel the game's central theme of self-loss. It transforms memory from a narrative concept into a tangible, consumable resource, deepening the emotional stakes of every encounter.
